ledger.claim: The rider's claim is properly before the tribunal on the platform's own records: the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00536, and the trace's first fix at 13:11:40 sits inside the record's own sequence (accepted 13:05:40, arrived 13:10:40, started 13:11:40), so limb (a) of the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is satisfied.

The rider's grievance is on the platform's own trip record, not merely in her statement: the record's dropoff label reads 'Marina Coastal Dr, 210 m short of the pier', and the driver's trace comes to rest 1.39 m from that recorded dropoff point (derived.driver_track.min_distance_m), so the vehicle stopped exactly where the record says it stopped - 210 m short of the pin the rider says she placed. The driver's own statement agrees on the distance ('I stopped at the closest legal stopping point... Two hundred metres').

The rider does not stretch the numbers and does not ask the tribunal to find a detour: the trace's own derived deviation is -0.11 km and -3.44%, because the vehicle covered LESS ground than the optimal route, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail and no excess-distance deviation exists on this record. The rider's complaint is the opposite shape - a trip terminated early - and the grievance is that she was billed the full 10.29 (base 3.80, distance 2.33, time 3.36, platform fee 0.80) for a trip the platform's own record says ended 210 m before her pin.

The driver's excuse - that the last stretch is a bus lane and he stopped at the closest legal stopping point - is a road-condition exoneration, and POL-RD-03 permits exoneration only where a traffic_advisory names the road, carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace reaches it, and is matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor; POL-RD-08 likewise provides that an assertion about traffic conditions unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID discharges nothing. No advisory exists in this pool: EV-ADVIS-00536-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window'). That artifact is disclosed as absent and, under POL-GEN-02, can carry no fact - so the driver's stated reason is corroborated by nothing in the record and he offers no clause-based ground for the stop.

The facts that would actually decide this dispute are carried by no artifact in the pool. trip_record.pickup_zone_class is null, so the zone-dependent arrival facts could not be computed at all - derived.arrival.available is false and the derivation records that no zone was substituted - leaving the record unable to say whether the vehicle reached a qualifying arrival at the pin. There is no rider track (derived.rider_presence.available false, fix_count 0), the chat log is empty (message_count 0, first_message_at null), and the trip record carries no venue_id for either endpoint and no in_app_calls, so the pin's exact location and any in-trip exchange are absent from the evidence; the rider does not rest her case on the parts of her account - including the messages she says she received - that this record does not carry.

ledger.claim: If the tribunal does find a deviation established on any view of the record, the refund is arithmetic rather than discretionary, and it should be run on the platform's own lines: under POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare is 9.24 against a charged_total of 10.29, a refund of 1.05, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and nowhere near the 90% full-refund share. The fare model on this trip is METERED with no quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 does not displace POL-RD-02.

The rider's profile cannot be used to discount her claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the corroboration gate in POL-RD-08 - which bites only at four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated - is not engaged, and no adverse inference on the strength of her filing history is available on this record.

The governing measurement shows no deviation at all. Under POL-RD-01 the excess is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (3.09 km) less optimal_distance_km (3.2 km) = -0.11 km, i.e. -3.44% of optimal. Both establishment tests must pass — excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute — and neither is met. No deviation is established, and the clause directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure wherever it disagrees with the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km, and this trace is unimpaired: 73 fixes, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, weight_multiplier 1.0. The 3.09 km trace figure is therefore the safe number to cite, and it sits below the 3.2 km booked optimal route.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. She cannot: the only admitted trace yields a negative excess, so the burden never shifts to the driver and the claim fails at its first step.

POL-RD-09(4) is the only refund route that operates whether or not a deviation exists, and it does not open on this fare: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0 and airport_surcharge is 0.0, so there is no unmatched gantry and no surcharge wrongly applied. Nothing within the SGD 10.29 charge is refundable independently of a deviation.

The in-app chat export for this trip contains zero messages. The record therefore carries no rider instruction that could have diverted the route and no message corroborating the rider's account of being repeatedly contacted. POL-RD-04 cannot be run for want of any waypoint_hint or named road, and nothing in the admitted chat supports a detour.

No pickup or dropoff amendment exists on the record: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-05 cannot be run, so no re-quoted optimal exists against which the driver's route could be measured, and the booked 3.2 km optimal stands as the baseline.

POL-RD-06 is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a material deviation, and none is recorded on this trip. For completeness, the driver's trailing record on the citable fields is clean — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250 — so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, so it can carry no fact for either side. There is accordingly no advisory or closure over the optimal corridor that could alter the POL-RD-03 baseline — and none is needed, because the trace records no excess distance in the first place.

ruling.explanation:
This is a route-deviation dispute, and the route-deviation test decides it. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement: the trace covers 3.09 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 3.2 km, an excess of -0.11 km (-3.44% of optimal). The trace is unimpaired (73 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, weight 1.0), so I used it rather than the rounded trip-record copy of 3.1 km. A deviation is established only if the excess exceeds 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km; the excess here is negative, so neither test is met and no deviation exists. POL-RD-01 then directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, and the fare stands as charged: SGD 10.29, being base 3.80 + distance 2.33 + time 3.36 + platform fee 0.80. No POL-RD-09(4) correction arises - erp_gantries is empty, tolls are 0.00 and no airport surcharge is applied, so there is no phantom line to refund - and because the fare breakdown's fare_model is METERED with no quoted fare, POL-RD-11 does not displace POL-RD-02. The POL-RD-02 recomputation the rider's brief offers (charged_total 10.29 less a recomputed 9.24 = 1.05) is never reached, because it runs only once a deviation is established, and no POL-RD-06 pattern check is triggered because no material deviation is recorded.

To the rider: what you describe is not disputed. The trip record itself labels the dropoff 'Marina Coastal Dr, 210 m short of the pier', the trace comes to rest 1.39 m from that recorded point, and the driver's own statement concedes 'Two hundred metres'. But that is a short-dropoff complaint, not a route deviation: the distance and time you were charged cover the 3.09 km actually driven, which is at or below the optimal route, and the route-deviation policy provides no refund for a dropoff short of the pin. Your point that the platform's messages did not reach you is uncorroborated here - the trip's chat export carries zero messages - and in any event it is not a ground for a refund under this policy. Your profile raises no adverse inference: deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration gate is not engaged.

To the driver: your explanation that the last stretch is a bus lane is a bare assertion - it cites no evidence ID, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no evidence carries no weight. It would not change the outcome in any case: there is no deviation for POL-RD-03 to exonerate, so that clause is not invoked against any absent artifact. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00536-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; I record that absence, but it carries no fact and no escalation follows from it.

POL-RD-10 does not fire: the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the timestamps are consistent, and the parties do not offer mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength - both agree the vehicle stopped about 200 m short. The zone-dependent arrival facts that could not be computed (pickup_zone_class is null) bear on thresholds that play no part in the excess-distance test that decides this case. The present payment state therefore stands.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
